definition: Wane means to grow gradually smaller, weaker, or dimmer.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word wane. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know wane should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By two in the morning the campfire had waned to a ring of orange embers, and the storytellers moved closer to be heard over the cold.
Dim is milder than wane — a dimmed lamp has lost some brightness once, while a waning one keeps losing more night after night.
Gutter is stronger than wane — a waning flame is shrinking but steady, while a guttering one lurches at the very edge of going out.

To ebb is to flow back and sink the way the tide does, and a tide that goes out is already owed back — strength, noise, or anger can ebb and then return within the hour. Wane borrows the moon instead: slow, phase-by-phase shrinking, with no quick return trip promised.

To dwindle is to shrink away bit by bit until almost nothing is left — supplies dwindle, crowds dwindle — and the arrow points one way, toward empty. Wane shares the slowness but not the destination: what wanes grows smaller or dimmer without necessarily heading for zero at all.

To fade is to lose color, sound, or presence softly until a thing thins toward invisibility, and what fades is usually gone for good. Wane is more measured: light, influence, or enthusiasm shrinking by slow degrees, still there each time you look, only a little less of it.
